data.description:
## Context

This ticket is **evidence-gathering and a proposal**, not an implementation. It tests whether a
defect pattern observed across one debugging session generalises, and asks whether rebar's review
gates should grow a new criterion for it. A well-argued **"no new criterion"** was an accepted
outcome of the investigation; the answer landed in between, and the narrowing is the contribution.

## The pattern, stated falsifiably

> **Additive obligation miss.** A change creates a new obligation — a contract, invariant, schema
> field, config key, changed default, new evidence kind, or a second site that must be kept in
> step — and discharges it at some of the sites that owe it but not all. The missed site is where
> the defect surfaces later.

To count as an instance, all three must be nameable:

1. **the obligation** — the specific contract/invariant/rule the change introduced or altered;
2. **the site(s) that DID discharge it** — at least one, in the same change;
3. **the site that did NOT** — and where the defect consequently surfaced.

**Falsifier:** if no site ever discharged the obligation, this is a missing guard or an incomplete
design, not an obligation miss. That clause is what stops the pattern from collapsing into "a bug
is when code is wrong". It is load-bearing — see the base rate below.

## Evidence

### Sample A — the 2026-08-20 session (NOT an independent sample)

These were all investigated in one session, under one protocol (`/rebar-debug`), by agents primed
by a shared prompt that named the pattern. Treat as hypothesis-generating only.

| alias | id | status | obligation | discharged at | missed at |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| perkish-balsamic-pupfish | `69b9-b740-c53a-4b56` | closed | administrative close dispositions as gate evidence | `close_precheck.py` (+164), `transition_close.py` (+29) | `gates.py` — sibling plan-review gate left blind |
| irongrey-chubby-oxpecker | `aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615` | closed | `add_comment` returns `{"id": …}` (asserted, never verified) | new consumer `_record_comment_id` | Cloud/ACLI transport returns a batch envelope with no id → dedup map permanently empty |
| moist-short-lionfish | `958e-f4b3-275c-4154` | closed | 20 ms write-path budget the change declared itself | drain-time use (original, correct) | `pending_enrichment` moved onto the WRITE path |
| electronic-deducible-maggot | `06f4-1c04-83c8-4a9f` | closed | test-distribution assumption | the new `--dist` default | tests relying on `xdist_group` |
| ruling-magnific-bats | `10d0-c26c-bdbb-4b1f` | closed | `add_dependency`'s closed-source guard + idempotency check | — (bypassed via `_write_link_event`) | both guard and idempotency check |
| brokendown-moonlit-kiskadee | `0276-7eea-baf0-48e3` | **open** | one verb, two help sources | help blob in `_commands/transition.py` | `_cli/help/transition.txt` — the file `--help` actually renders |
| itchy-arbored-peccary | `3907-0110-7688-43bd` | closed | ADR 0005 D5 "backstopped by the byte total" | — (no ticket ever obliged it) | never implemented; second populate path added to a store whose accounting contract existed |
| steep-tired-whimbrel | `f5c4-b2d1-4503-4bfe` | in_progress | gate-off vs config-unreadable are distinct states | gate-off skip | fail-open config-unreadable skip collapsed a fault into a policy choice |
| bediasite-bilineate-stoat | `fb8b-189d-97ab-4546` | closed | remedy advertised by a gate message | the message | collides with a sibling gate shipped seven weeks earlier |
| conscious-weighable-spittlebug | `3198-438c-72a5-470f` | closed | detached child needs a durable `cwd=` | — (never right anywhere) | **all three** spawn sites |
| nuclear-calm-heron | `da68-fc7c-068c-4c53` | **open** | drain lock must serialise a shared store | — | worktree-local `.rebar` → two worktrees hold different locks |
| afeard-technical-kodiakbear | `2dc4-9bcd-75b9-4544` | **open** | (consolidation follow-up to spittlebug) | — | — |

Instances 1 and 5 were verified independently against git rather than taken on trust:
`9844f6de35` touches `close_precheck.py`/`transition_close.py` and **no** `gates.py`;
`0f999860ad` touches `_commands/transition.py` and **not** `_cli/help/transition.txt` — while the
*earlier* `9844f6de35` updated **both** help sources, so the pair was demonstrably maintained
before it drifted.

### Sample B — independent instances (random sample, blind to the pattern)

45 closed bugs drawn at random (seed 20260820) from the 704-ticket closed-bug corpus and
classified by an agent given the definition but **not** the session's instances. 16 qualified.
A representative selection, each with all three clauses nameable:

| alias | obligation | discharged at | missed at |
|---|---|---|---|
| chanceful-microbial-fallowdeer | terminal-blocker status vocabulary | `_unblock.py`, `_graph.py` (`closed,deleted`), `next_batch.py` | `_ready.py` — `closed` only; `ready` and `next-batch` disagree |
| said-stilt-brow | "any mutating mode is gated" under `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` | the `"live"` string check | other non-zero-cap modes in `MODE_CAPS` — bootstrap-strict/throttle mutate real Jira |
| vapoury-attack-lamb | surface a failed tickets push to the caller (bug 2a76) | CLI/sync path | async `Popen(stderr=DEVNULL)`, library `NullHandler`, MCP tool result, reconciler logger |
| asbestos-lithe-kouprey | new `unlink … [relation]` contract | `unlink.txt`, `cli-reference.md`, `user-guide.md` | `overview.txt`, `ticket-model.md`, `event-schema.md` |
| craven-oppressed-galago / aphidian-unartful-hound | migrated `compute_mutations(local_state, …)` contract | the migration documented in `differ.py` | sole production caller `run_differs.py:222` — aged-out key planned as a resurrect-CREATE |
| terse-frost-ale | no mutation under `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` | the `recover=True` gate, other read tools | plain `fsck()` / `ticket-fsck.sh:180` deletes a stale `index.lock` |
| handwoven-unthankful-reindeer | case-insensitive project-key comparison | `applier._cross_project_targets` (`.upper()`) | `outbound_differ._compute_outbound_create_mutation` |
| cranial-sulfur-peafowl | parent-first cascade invariant | `open→in_progress` in claim/transition | the `closed→open` edge in `reopen` |
| printed-woeful-queenant | "both stages resolve the same repo root" (asserted in a docstring) | `overlay.py` | `prompts.py::get_prompt` |
| unrational-fusible-godwit | cursor-stall guard (`SilentTruncationError`) | `fetcher._iter_pages` | three `acli_graph.py` whole-project readers |
| enhanced-panoramic-armedcrab | inward/outward → relation direction mapping | outbound write path | `_diff_links_inbound` + `_diff_link_removals` |
| autumnal-defectible-xeme | tolerate empty/absent date bounds | git/churn readers | `event_metrics._bounds` → `fromisoformat("")` |
| flap-meal-boast | documented `--opt <value>` space form | composer/write cmds, `_cmd_ready` | `reads_cli.py` `_cmd_session_logs`/`_cmd_list` |
| moldavite-evasive-elephant | assert on signals the invoked route emits | route gating in `__main__.py` | the two assertion helpers re-pointed at `sync` |
| shockproof-twill-porpoise | host-independence fixture control | sibling `test_metric_backend_skip_is_reconstructable` | `test_full_backend_account_is_present` |

**The pattern generalises.** 16 independent instances, none from the session, none from its
protocol. Also independently confirmed: `accepted-androgenic-elk` (`0024-fa99-d5bb-49bc`) —
`_metric_invoke` omitted scc `--by-file` while `_scc_files` parsed per-file entries, and the
*sibling* consumer `metrics/analyzers/scc_loc.py` had already been fixed under
`rapid-cuboid-velvetcrab` while the grounding consumer stayed unaudited.

### The copy-propagation variant (a different mechanism)

`conscious-weighable-spittlebug` is **not** an obligation miss. Verified from history: the missing
`cwd=` originates in `57114212cf` (2026-06-12, `_store/push.py`), was copied to
`d2dea317ec` (2026-08-13, `compact_trigger.py`) and `9ad46965bd` (2026-07-09, `enrich_drain.py`),
and all three were fixed together in `d575600381`. No contract changed; an original omission was
**deliberately imitated** three times. The reviewers of copies 2 and 3 had the strongest available
correctness signal — the code matched existing, shipped, working code.

This matters in both directions and the story records both:

- **For the thesis:** it is a mechanism by which one missed site becomes N, and a
  "did you update every consumer?" check would miss it entirely, because there is no producer
  change to trigger one.
- **Against a simple criterion:** "prior art in the repo is not evidence of correctness" is far
  harder to operationalise than "update your consumers". A reviewer cannot re-derive every pattern
  a change imitates. `/rebar-debug` Phase 2 Step 5 has a prior-art trust check, but it only
  excludes code *"under an open bug or a recent CI/test failure"* — `push.py` was under neither, so
  even that check would have passed. **No proposal here covers this variant.**

Also recorded honestly, correcting the framing brief: for this defect the fix site **is** the cause
site and there was no good→bad transition, because the site was never right. That is a genuine
counter-example to "the fix site is not the cause site", not something to smooth over.

## Adversarial analysis

### Base rate — measured, n=45

| bucket | count | share |
|---|---|---|
| A — obligation miss | 16 | **35.6%** |
| B — not an obligation miss | 28 | 62.2% |
| C — unclassifiable | 1 | 2.2% |

Among the A's: **13 cross-file (81%)**, 3 same-file.

**Definition sensitivity is the headline result.** Requiring a nameable commit that created the
obligation drops it to ~24% (the *divergent-duplicate* shapes — `flap-meal-boast`,
`autumnal-defectible-xeme`, `chanceful-microbial-fallowdeer`, `unrational-fusible-godwit` — have no
dated producer change). Loosening to "someone should have kept two things in sync" pushes it past
**60%**. So the pattern is discriminating **only under the strict three-clause definition**, and a
criterion that does not encode all three clauses will fire on most of the corpus. Clear non-fits:
`fond-ulna-ball` (cache key is `name:size`; one wrong key composition, no second site),
`teenyweeny-courteous-goldeneye` (review-bot re-selects abandoned changes forever; nobody ever
conceived the obligation), `caressive-noteworthy-goldfish` (missing PEP 503 normalisation inside a
single comparison helper).

### The project has already measured this class — and it over-fires

`docs/plan-review-gate.md:263-269` reports, from plan-v3 field evidence over **18,085 verified
findings**, a named class: *"omitted scope site / unenumerated consumer"*, **1,307 findings**, of
which the verifier graded **~90% (1,173) as `none`**. It further records that a blunt widening
*"would have routed 113 corpus findings into the 0.85 floor at once (4.3% of runs flipping
PASS→BLOCK), the same over-fire the oracle split had to walk back."*

This is the strongest single argument in this ticket, and it argues **against** a broad criterion.
Reviewers already surface this class constantly; the verifier judges ~9 in 10 immaterial.

### Selection effects (three, all real)

1. Sample A is one session, one protocol, one shared prompt naming the pattern. Not independent.
2. Only **65 `caused_by` edges exist across all 704 closed bugs** (<10%). Origin attribution is
   recorded almost exclusively when `/rebar-debug` traces it, so "how often did a traceable origin
   change miss a site?" is under-measured by construction across the corpus.
3. Sample B is drawn from *closed, investigated* bugs, which skews toward tickets with a written
   RCA — bucket A is the one requiring three specific nameable things, so its rate would likely be
   lower in a corpus with weaker investigation records.

### Every origin commit predates the closest existing control

`code-review-surface-parity` shipped **2026-08-19**. The origin commits are `2026-06-12`,
`2026-07-09`, `2026-07-13`, `2026-08-12`, `2026-08-13`, `2026-08-14`, `2026-08-15`. **All of them
predate it.** Sample A therefore *cannot* demonstrate a gap in the current review stack; it
demonstrates a gap in the stack as it was. Any proposal must be justified on the *shape* of the
misses under today's triggers, not on the mere existence of these bugs. Empirically checked via
`registry.glob_triggered_overlays`: `surface-parity` glob-fires on `9844f6de35`, `0f999860ad` and
`d575600381` today — and would still miss all three, because its prompt confines the sibling set to
the lib/CLI/MCP adapter triple, while the actual missed siblings were `gates.py`, a help `.txt`,
and three unrelated spawn sites.

### Actionability

A criterion saying "update all consumers" is unactionable unless the consumer set is discoverable.
It is: `code-review-deletion-impact` and `code-review-surface-parity` both give the reviewer
`search_files` / `read_file` (AST/LSP where available) and instruct a **one-hop** sweep, and
`project.symbol-reference-completeness` routes call-site inventories through Serena. Discovery is a
solved problem here; **trigger scope, not discoverability, is the constraint.**

### Portability

Satisfied by construction. Plan-review and code-review criteria are LLM overlays over a plan/diff
plus repo read tools, declared in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` with a prompt in
`.rebar/prompts/`. No CI provider is involved, so nothing here trips `project.portability`
(which requires a named alternate client shape, a causal failure mechanism and an observable
breakage — none arises for an in-process overlay).

## Does an existing criterion already cover this? Partly — cited

Enumerated all **49** plan-review criteria (`registry.load_criteria()`) and all **14** code-review
overlays (`llm/code_review/registry.py`). Findings:

| mechanism | what it covers | posture | why it misses this class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `omits_required_site` (grade, not criterion) | *"the plan's scope or file list OMITS a site the change provably MUST touch"* — 0.85 floor, HARD-OVERRIDE auto-high | **blocking** | It is a **grading axis**, not a hunter. It can only grade a finding some other criterion already produced. |
| `T13` behavioral-prohibition consumer scan | translates a **new prohibition** into greps over existing call sites; triages MIGRATED / EXEMPTED / **UNCOVERED**; fail-open when not grep-reducible | advisory | Trigger is *prohibition* only ("block/reject/require-before/enforce"). Every instance here was an **addition**. |
| `code-review-deletion-impact` | **removed/renamed** symbols → surviving dangling references, one hop, auto-fires | (overlay) | Covers the **subtractive** blast radius. There is no additive mirror. |
| `code-review-surface-parity` | write-op param/guard/required-field changed on one adapter without siblings; globs `**/_commands/**`, `**/_lib_writes.py`, `**/_mcp_writes.py` | (overlay) | Sibling set is a **hardcoded triple**. None of the actual missed siblings is one of the three. |
| `project.symbol-reference-completeness` | a plan that names a symbol **and enumerates** a call-site list → check completeness via Serena | **advisory** | Gated on a plan enumerating a list for a *named symbol*. `gates.py`, a help `.txt`, a latency budget, `xdist_group`, an ADR promise are not symbol references. |
| `asserted-capability` | plan asserts named module M provides capability C and depends on it | **advisory** | Covers the **consumer-side** direction ("does what I depend on exist?"). The producer-side direction ("I changed this — who depends on it?") has no criterion. |
| `G7` leaf-parent containment | leaf scope ⊄ parent's plan | blocking | Scoped to leaf-vs-parent, not code siblings. |
| `T12(c)` deploy ordering | producers/consumers deploy order | advisory | Rollout ordering, not site completeness. |
| `/rebar-debug` Axis-2 parity sweep | NAME THE RULE (without naming the fixed site) → five-slot CHANNEL CENSUS → PER-SURFACE PROBE (`path:line` or **MISSING**) → forced DISPOSITION | — | **Debug time only.** It runs *after* a bug exists. This is the fully-specified, proven procedure the proposal wants to run earlier. |

**Verdict on coverage:** the concept is *not* novel to rebar — the project has independently
converged on it three times (T13, `deletion-impact`, `surface-parity`) and encodes it as a blocking
*grade*. The residual gap is narrow and specific:

> **An ADDITIVE obligation owed to a NON-ADAPTER sibling has no review-time hunter.**
> Subtraction is covered (`deletion-impact`). The adapter triple is covered (`surface-parity`).
> Prohibitions are covered (`T13`). Additions to arbitrary siblings are not.

## Proposal

Given the ~90% immateriality rate on this class, a broad "did you update every consumer?" criterion
is **not** warranted and this ticket recommends against it. Instead, two narrow moves, in order:

**P1 (primary) — a project code-review overlay `project.obligation-parity`,** built as the
**additive mirror of `deletion-impact`**, reusing T13's triage verbatim:

1. From the diff's **added** lines, identify each new obligation of a *closed, enumerable* kind
   only: a new enum/literal member branched on elsewhere; a new required field or config key; a
   changed default; a new evidence kind consumed by a named registry; a new guard on one of several
   parallel entry points.
2. Reduce it to a grep signature; enumerate existing sites via `search_files`/`read_file`.
3. Triage each: **MIGRATED / EXEMPTED / UNCOVERED**. Only UNCOVERED is a finding.
4. **Fail-open/abstain** when the obligation is not reducible to a checkable pattern — never
   fabricate sites (T13's rule, which is what keeps this off "everything").
5. Ship **advisory**, glob-triggered, `applies_to` declared in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`.

Anti-fire guards, mirroring the four-element threshold `project.portability` uses: a finding
requires **(a)** the cited added line carrying the obligation, **(b)** a `path:line` of a site that
DID discharge it in the same diff, **(c)** a `path:line` of a site that did NOT, and **(d)** the
observable consequence of leaving it. Missing any one ⇒ no finding. This is exactly the strict
three-clause definition, which is what drove the base rate from >60% down to ~24-36%.

**P2 (cheaper, do first if only one lands) — widen `T13`'s trigger lexicon from *prohibition* to
*obligation*.** T13's machinery already does the whole job; only its trigger sentence is narrow.
This is a prompt edit, not new infrastructure.

**Explicitly out of scope:** the copy-propagation variant. Nothing proposed here detects it, and
this ticket does not claim otherwise.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A ruling is recorded on P1 and P2 — **adopt, adopt-narrowed, or reject** — with reasons.
- [ ] Any adopted criterion ships **advisory** first and is **not** promoted to blocking without a
      calibration replay showing its fire rate on the existing corpus, explicitly compared against
      the recorded ~90%-`none` rate for the "omitted scope site / unenumerated consumer" class.
- [ ] The criterion (if adopted) encodes all four evidence elements (a)-(d); a prompt lacking any
      of them is rejected at review.
- [ ] The criterion is replayed against at least 5 of the origin commits named here
      (`9844f6de35`, `0f999860ad`, `27b868ba55`, `746c1ba2e9`, `f943c7ef58`) and its hit/miss
      recorded per commit — a criterion that catches none of them is not worth shipping.
- [ ] False-positive exposure is measured on a sample of recent PASSing changes and recorded in
      `docs/code-review-fp-ledger.md`.
- [ ] No CI provider is required to trigger it (`project.portability` clean).
- [ ] If rejected, the reasons are written into `docs/plan-review-gate.md` beside the existing
      plan-v3 field-evidence paragraph, so the next investigator finds the ruling rather than
      re-deriving this analysis.

## Verification

Analysis-only ticket. Verification is the ruling plus, if adopted, the calibration replay and
FP-ledger entry named above. No source change is proposed by this ticket itself.
data.title: Rule on an additive-obligation parity criterion for review time (evidence + proposal)
